note: $dev is an explicit-invocation orchestrator in Codex. Prompts name it directly. expected_behavior describes a good orchestration run, not a code artifact.

evals.name: build-vs-buy-iso8601-duration
evals.prompt: 用 $dev 走一遍：我在一个 TS 项目里要加个函数，把 ISO 8601 duration 字符串（像 PT1H30M、P3DT4H、PT0.5S）解析成总秒数。
expected_behavior: Runs the Step 0 dependency preflight before anything else
Uses the current harness checklist for preflight and does not run a generic dependency script

In Codex, accepts the visible context7:context7-mcp skill plus its declared MCP dependency as preflight evidence; does not require raw Context7 tool names to be eagerly listed, but stops if the first required lookup fails

Grills with exactly one question per turn, starting with the highest-uncertainty question whose answer is most likely to change the next question, scope, or acceptance criteria (for example whether months/years must map to fixed seconds before asking about smaller syntax cases)
Makes an EXPLICIT build-vs-buy decision via managing-dependencies (weighs a maintained lib like tinyduration / iso8601-duration vs a hand-rolled regex) rather than silently hand-rolling

Invokes pm-execution:test-scenarios with PRODUCT, USER_STORY, and CONTEXT before writing code, then writes the approved scenarios next to the ADR as <adr-stem>.test-scenarios.md, or to <target-project-root>/docs/dev/<run-slug>/test-scenarios.md when no ADR exists
Delegates implementation to a subagent; the orchestrator itself does not write the feature code
Passes the exact scenario contract path and the TDD skill edge to the implementation subagent, and asks it to update scenario status/evidence

Before implementation, asks whether to use mattpocock-skills:to-spec and personal-voice for a collaborator-facing proposal; if accepted, asks for the destination path in the next turn, writes Before vs. After and Pros and Cons sections plus workflow and architecture diagrams, and waits for approval
Stops instead of continuing when required dependencies such as subagent delegation or ponytail are missing
Delegates review to a separate review subagent; the review subagent must invoke the review skill edge and may run controlled validation but must not edit source files
Spawns a separate fix subagent only for findings the orchestrator judges valid and worth fixing now
Pauses (or states an explicit assumption) at each gate

evals.name: bugfix-csv-quoting
evals.prompt: $dev pipeline 修个 bug：我们导出 CSV 时，如果某个字段里本身含逗号、双引号或换行，导出的文件就会错列/串行。
expected_behavior: Runs preflight first
Stops and reports the exact failed check when the current harness is missing a required capability; does not emulate the missing skill inline
Grills for the real contract (RFC 4180? which consumers read the file? expected quoting?) and finds the root cause (missing field quoting/escaping), not just the reported symptom
Build-vs-buy leans toward a battle-tested CSV serializer (csv-stringify / papaparse) over hand-rolled escaping, given how many quoting edge cases exist

Uses the test-scenarios skill edge to write the scenario contract before code, using the ADR-adjacent path when an ADR exists or <target-project-root>/docs/dev/<run-slug>/test-scenarios.md otherwise, covering embedded comma, embedded double-quote (must be doubled), embedded newline, leading/trailing whitespace, empty field, unicode
Delegates implementation to a subagent, then delegates review to a separate subagent before deciding whether to spawn a fix subagent

evals.name: larger-feature-oauth
evals.prompt: run $dev to add Google OAuth login to my Next.js app
expected_behavior: Runs preflight first
In Codex, uses the Codex checklist and must not tell the user to restart Claude Code
Grills heavily (which auth library? session storage? existing user model? callback URLs? what 'login' must gate) and surfaces that this is large and may need scoping before code
Build-vs-buy strongly favors a mature library (Auth.js / next-auth) over hand-rolling an OAuth flow, for security reasons
Writes an ADR-adjacent <adr-stem>.test-scenarios.md before code with scenarios including error and security cases (state/CSRF param, token refresh, denied consent, callback errors)
Before implementation, offers the optional reviewable proposal document and continues without it when the user declines
Delegates implementation to a subagent; does not try to one-shot the whole feature in the main thread
Keeps review and fix responsibilities separated across different subagents
Uses gates to keep a fuzzy, large task from running away
